primary_issue: Does not read as an explosion: missing the core explosion signatures (hot emissive flash, volumetric fire/smoke, dense fine debris/embers, and strong interactive lighting), so the shot plays like a cool, low-energy glass break.
issues: Effect/type mismatch: the render reads as broken glass in an interior room, not an explosion event (no fireball, smoke plume, or shock-lit environment).
No volumetrics: absence of smoke/fire volume removes the main mass/silhouette expected from an explosion.
No high-intensity emissive core or bloom/glare: nothing drives a bright flash or HDR highlight structure.
Lighting doesn’t react to a blast: walls/floor/objects lack warm bounce and sharp flash-driven contrast; overall image remains cool and evenly lit.
Glass material response is unconvincing for fast energetic shatter: shards look uniformly thin/flat with limited refraction/thickness cues; highlights are not varied enough.
No motion cues: shards are razor-sharp (no motion blur/camera shake), reducing perceived speed/energy.
Aliasing on thin shard edges/high-contrast lines (stair-stepping/jaggies), especially noticeable on small fragments.
Weak grounding/contact: some contact shadows feel too soft/low-contrast for a strong flash; fragments don’t feel heavy/embedded in the space.
Composition lacks a strong focal ‘blast center’: the event is small/distant and contrast is muted, so the eye isn’t pulled to an explosive origin point.
Missing secondary details: no dust cloud, micro-particulates, embers/sparks, soot/scorch, or debris spread that typically sells an explosion.
suggestions: If you must stay within the current script’s adjustable params, push the shot toward a flash-driven look: increase World/background intensity (Line 86: bg Strength from 0.06 → ~0.15–0.35) and shift background color warmer (Line 85: bg Color from deep blue to a warmer dark brown/charcoal) so added emission/lighting can read as a warm event instead of a cool room.
Make the emissive component read hotter: adjust emission color (Line 470: emission Color) toward orange/yellow (e.g., RGB ~ (1.0, 0.5, 0.15)) so any glow elements stop reading as cold/neutral.
Reduce “procedural brick” dominance if it distracts from the event: lower brick contrast/saturation (Lines 380–382) so the environment doesn’t compete with the shatter/explosion focal point.

Increase micro-surface breakup to help specular variation (subtle): raise bump strength slightly (Line 427: 0.07 → 0.10–0.14) and/or reduce bump distance (Line 428: 0.02 → 0.01–0.015) to avoid overly broad, plastic-looking shading on surfaces.

For a true explosion, add elements not currently present in this parameter set: (1) volumetric smoke/fire (density + temperature-driven emission), (2) embers/sparks particle layer, (3) dust micro-particles, and (4) a short-duration high-intensity flash light that casts warm shadows/highlights.

Render/comp improvements: enable motion blur (object/vector), add bloom/glare in comp, raise samples/AA for thin geometry (glass edges), and consider a Filmic tonemap with higher contrast so highlights can punch without clipping.
Reframe tighter on the break/explosion origin (or add DOF) to create a clear focal point and improve perceived scale/energy.
vision_assessment: The image shows an interior room with a centered window area and scattered glass shards/fragments. Lighting is predominantly cool and even, with muted contrast. There is no visible fireball, smoke plume, or volumetric density that would form an explosion silhouette; no hot core or bright flash that would cast warm interactive light onto walls/floor/objects. Shards are crisp with no motion blur, which makes the event feel slow/static. Thin glass edges exhibit noticeable aliasing/jaggies, and the scene overall reads as a clean glass break set in a room rather than an energetic explosion with secondary debris, dust, embers, and HDR glow.
